name: Botvee AI Agent
author: Botvee

sections.description:
Botvee AI Agent is the official WordPress connector for the Botvee AI Agent platform.

This lightweight plugin connects your WordPress website directly with your Botvee account. No coding, no FTP, no theme editing required — just install, connect, and your AI Agent is live.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Click Connect with Botvee
  3. Log into your Botvee account
  4. Select which AI Agent to display
  5. Your AI Agent is live instantly!

Key Features

  • One-Click Connection — OAuth-style authentication, no manual token pasting
  • AI Agent Selector — Choose which AI Agent appears on your site from a searchable dropdown
  • Auto Widget Injection — AI Agent widget loads automatically on your pages
  • Display Rules — Show the AI Agent everywhere, only on selected pages, or everywhere except the pages you choose
  • Activity Panel — Conversations, messages and leads without leaving WordPress
  • Agent Health — See at a glance if your AI Agent is untrained, paused, or deleted on Botvee
  • WooCommerce — Live product, stock and order lookups, plus optional browse-abandonment and cart-recovery tracking
  • Ultra Lightweight — Under 1MB, minimal database usage, async loading
  • Fully Managed — All AI logic, training, and customization stays on Botvee’s platform
  • Secure — Encrypted token storage, nonce validation, capability checks

What This Plugin Does NOT Do

This plugin is a connector only. It does not store chats, process AI, manage training data, or render the AI Agent widget. All intelligence lives on botvee.ai.

External services

This plugin is a connector for Botvee, an external AI Agent service run by Botvee (https://botvee.ai). The plugin cannot work without it: all AI logic, agent training, conversation storage and the chat widget itself live on Botvee’s servers, not on your site.

It talks to two Botvee hosts:

  • https://botvee.ai — where the chat widget script (/widget.js) is loaded from on your public pages, and where the dashboard links in this plugin point.
  • https://api.botvee.ai — the API this plugin sends requests to, and where you sign in to authorise the connection.

What is sent, and when:

  1. When you click “Connect with Botvee” — a sign-in window opens on api.botvee.ai. On success your site domain, the chosen AI Agent id and whether WooCommerce is active on this site are registered with Botvee (so the AI Agent only offers product and order lookups on a WooCommerce store), and an access token is stored (encrypted) on your site. Whether WooCommerce is active is sent again once a day and whenever WooCommerce is activated or deactivated. Nothing is sent before you click Connect.
  2. On every page where the AI Agent is shown — the visitor’s browser loads the widget script from botvee.ai and sends the AI Agent id, your site domain, an anonymous visitor id, and, for logged-in users only, their display name, email address, and (with WooCommerce) their order count and total spent. This is what lets the agent answer “where is my order?” for a signed-in customer.
  3. While you use the plugin dashboard — your AI Agent list, conversation/message/lead counts and agent status are fetched from the API.
  4. After you connect, if WooCommerce is active — your published products, and your orders (number, status, payment status and method, total, items, the customer’s name, email and phone, the shipping and billing address, and the courier tracking number once shipped), are sent to Botvee so the AI Agent can answer questions about stock, prices, order status and delivery, and so you can see each order in the Botvee dashboard. An order is sent again whenever it changes. Product stock changes are sent as they happen so Stock Alert customers are notified.
  5. After you connect, on any WordPress site — your published pages (title, link and text; password-protected pages are never sent) are sent to Botvee so the AI Agent can answer questions about your policies, shipping, contact details and anything else on them. A page is sent again when it is edited, and removed from Botvee when it is unpublished or deleted.
  6. When you edit an order in the Botvee dashboard (WooCommerce) — Botvee calls this site’s REST endpoint /wp-json/botvee/v1/order-update, authenticated with the secret exchanged when you connected, to change the order’s status or shipping address, add an order note, or save a courier tracking number. Botvee also adds private order notes when it records a tracking number or a new courier status. Nothing on the order changes unless you make the edit in your own dashboard (or turn courier tracking on).
  7. Only if you switch them on — Browse abandonment sends the viewed product, view duration, an anonymous visitor id and the shopper’s email/phone; Cart recovery sends the cart contents and the shopper’s email/phone. Both are off by default, and even when on, nothing is sent for a shopper who has not given an email address or phone number. You can switch them off at any time under Botvee → WooCommerce → Send shopper activity to Botvee.

By using this plugin you agree to Botvee’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Terms of Service: https://botvee.ai/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://botvee.ai/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the botvee-ai-agent folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu
  3. Navigate to Botvee in the left sidebar
  4. Click Connect with Botvee and follow the prompts
sections.faq:
Do I need a Botvee account?

Yes. Create a free account at botvee.ai to get started.

Does the plugin slow down my site?

No. The widget script loads asynchronously and does not block page rendering.

Can I control which pages the AI Agent appears on?

Yes. Under Where it appears you can show it on every page, only on pages you pick, or everywhere except the pages you pick. WooCommerce stores can also hide it on checkout and account pages.

Can I use different AI Agents on different pages?

One AI Agent is active per site. You can change which one at any time from the dashboard.

What does WooCommerce tracking send?

Only shoppers who have already given an email address or phone number are sent, because both features follow up by email or phone. Both toggles are off until you switch them on. Requests are non-blocking, so they never slow a page down.

Is my data secure?

Yes. Authentication tokens are encrypted using AES-256 before storage. All API communication uses HTTPS.

My store has thousands of products — will they all reach Botvee?

Yes. The catalog is exported in chunks of 1,000 products (20 pages of 50), with a 30-minute rest between chunks, and it resumes from the page it reached until the last product. A store with 16,000 products therefore completes in roughly 10 hours of background runs. The page reached is remembered, so a missed WP-Cron run continues from there instead of starting over. “Sync now” starts the first chunk immediately; the rest continues on their own. On a site with no traffic, WP-Cron only runs when someone visits — add a real cron job (wp cron event run --due-now) if the store is very quiet.
sections.changelog:
1.3.2

  • Fixed: on the block-based checkout (WooCommerce’s default) an order placed after a chat add-to-cart reached Botvee with no attribution, so Sales by AI showed nothing. The chat cookies are now also read when the Store API places the order
  • New: an order WooCommerce itself attributes to Botvee (Orders → Origin “Source: Botvee”, from the utm_source every chat link carries) counts as a chat sale even when the cookie was not read
  • Fixed: the 30-minute rest between catalog chunks was skipped on the next page load, and a second export walk could start next to the first and send the same products again. The check for a queued export now sees steps queued for any page
  • Fixed: the daily reconcile could restart a catalog export from page 1 while one was still running
  • Fixed: after “Sync now” the background export skipped one page (products 1,001-1,050) and continued from the page after it
  • Changed: the first background chunk is now a full 20 pages (1,000 products), like every chunk after it

1.3.1

  • New: Sales by AI — when a shopper adds a product to the cart or opens a product from the chat, the widget leaves two cookies (botvee_src, botvee_sess). At checkout the order is stamped with the chat session that led to it (_botvee_session, next to the existing _botvee_source), and both are sent to Botvee with the order. The dashboard’s Sales by AI page can then show the order next to the conversation it came from
  • New: on WooCommerce stores the plugin passes the store’s checkout URL to the chat widget, so the “Checkout” button in the chat opens this store’s own checkout page
  • Changed: the order push to Botvee carries attributionSession (empty for orders that did not come through the chat)

1.3.0

  • Fixed: catalogs larger than 1,000 products stopped at 1,000. “Sync now” walks at most 20 pages of 50 products inside one request (a bigger walk would pass PHP’s time limit), but it then recorded the catalog as synced — so the daily reconcile saw “done” and the remaining pages were never sent. A store with 16,000 products showed 1,000 forever
  • New: catalog export now runs in chunks — 20 pages (1,000 products), a 30-minute rest, then the next 20 pages, resuming from where it stopped until the last page. A 16,000-product store finishes in roughly ten hours of background runs instead of stopping at 1,000
  • New: the page the export reached is remembered, so a dropped WP-Cron event resumes from there instead of starting over at page 1
  • Fixed: “Sync now” no longer reports the catalog as complete when the page bound stopped the walk; it hands the next page to the background export and only marks it complete at the real end of the catalog
  • Fixed: switching to a different AI Agent, and the daily reconcile, both reset the resume point so the new agent’s catalog is exported from page 1

1.2.9

  • Fixed: orders, stock and product changes are now sent to Botvee from a background job, never from the shopper’s checkout or the admin’s save — a slow or unreachable Botvee no longer holds up the store. A failed push is retried later without filling the site’s cron list, and the catalog export pauses instead of queueing every page during an outage
  • New: each order’s shipping and billing address is sent to Botvee, for the order page in the dashboard
  • New: any change to an order in wp-admin (address, items, total, note, tracking) reaches Botvee at once, not only status changes
  • New: orders can be edited from the Botvee dashboard (status, shipping address, order note, courier tracking) and the change is saved on this store
  • New: every published page (privacy, refund, shipping, about, contact…) is sent to Botvee so the AI answers from it; works on WordPress sites without WooCommerce too
  • New: the plugin tells Botvee whether the site runs WooCommerce (on connect, daily, and the moment WooCommerce is switched on or off), so the AI only offers product and order search on real stores
  • New: a tracking number saved from Botvee, and every new courier status Botvee reads, is added to the order as a private note — so stores without a shipment-tracking plugin can see the parcel’s progress in wp-admin
  • New: with Advanced Shipment Tracking or WooCommerce Shipment Tracking installed, a tracking number saved from Botvee is also added to that plugin’s shipment list (its order screen and customer emails)

1.2.8

  • New: when an order ships, its courier tracking number (Shipment Tracking, Advanced Shipment Tracking and other plugins that save it on the order) is sent to Botvee, so the AI can answer “where is my order?” and message the customer when the parcel moves

1.2.7

  • Fixed: on a store with a refund, the one-time order history export stopped with a PHP fatal error (“Call to undefined method OrderRefund::get_order_number”) and WordPress emailed the site owner. Refunds are no longer treated as orders

1.2.6

  • Fixed: the one-time order history export could restart from the newest order on every page load and never finish, re-sending the same orders to Botvee for days. It now remembers how far it got, works in short runs that fit the host’s PHP time limit, and stops once the history is exported

1.2.5

  • New: Position on screen — choose whether the chat button sits on the left or the right, at the top or the bottom, and how far it sits from each edge (0–300px). Useful when a cookie bar, a back-to-top button or a sticky cart already owns the bottom-right corner
  • New: the greeting bubble follows the button, and its pointer and close button move to the matching corner
  • Changed: the chat window opens towards the middle of the screen, so it never runs off the edge the button is parked against
  • Changed: the position is written onto the button itself, not only in the stylesheet — the chat script pins its own bottom-right corner, so a right or bottom distance had no effect until now
  • Note: on a phone the chat still opens full screen; only the button moves
  • Note: sites that never change the position get exactly what they had — no extra CSS or script is added

1.2.4

  • Changed: the AI Agent panel now shows the agent that is connected to this site as a single card, with a Change button — the full list only appears when you want to switch
  • Changed: picking an agent from the list no longer saves it straight away; the choice is applied when you click Save (or discarded with Cancel)
  • New: Save asks you to confirm. If the agent you picked is already connected to another website or Shopify store, the confirmation names that site and tells you it will be disconnected there before it is connected here; otherwise it is a plain “are you sure”
  • Changed: the agent list from Botvee now carries where each agent is currently connected, which is what the confirmation reads

1.2.3

  • Changed: browse-abandonment and cart-recovery tracking are now off by default — nothing about a shopper is sent to Botvee until you switch them on yourself
  • Changed: the browse-abandonment timer is a proper enqueued script instead of markup printed into the footer
  • New: an “External services” section in this readme setting out exactly what is sent to Botvee, when, and links to the terms and privacy policy
  • Changed: the plugin now talks to botvee.ai and api.botvee.ai

1.2.2

  • Changed: the Connection panel now sits under the AI Agent picker, filling the empty column that was left below it
  • Fixed: the dashboard logo URL is escaped where it is printed instead of where it is assigned
  • Changed: admin template variables carry the full botvee_ prefix, so they cannot collide with another plugin’s globals
  • Changed: display-rule modes are written as class constants rather than bare strings
  • Changed: the WP_DEBUG-only proxy log line is marked as intentional for code scanners
  • Changed: readme “Tested up to” raised to 7.0 and the stable tag brought in step with the plugin version

1.2.1

  • Fixed: switching to a different AI Agent left the new agent with an empty catalog — the pushed store mirror now follows the site to whichever agent it points at

1.2.0

  • New: the plugin pushes your full product catalog to Botvee, so the AI Agent answers from a mirror instead of waiting on a live site call — with a sync-status line and a “Sync now” button on the dashboard
  • New: every WooCommerce order is pushed with its payment state, so customer and spend figures on Botvee reflect paid orders only
  • New: restocks are pushed the moment they happen, so Stock Alerts go out instantly instead of on the next cron sweep
  • Changed: the pushed mirror is now the primary source for product answers, with the live store proxy kept as the fallback

1.1.4

  • Fixed: buyers could still receive an abandoned-cart nudge after checking out — the order confirmation now closes every cart captured for that shopper, including ones captured by the chat widget under a different id
  • Fixed: browse-abandonment tracking never fired — dwell time is now measured in the browser instead of being reported as zero
  • Fixed: disconnecting now clears the WooCommerce proxy secret, so the site’s product/order endpoints stop accepting the old credentials
  • Changed: readme stable tag brought back in step with the plugin version

1.1.0

  • New: display rules — choose which pages the AI Agent appears on, and hide it on WooCommerce checkout and account pages
  • New: activity panel showing conversations, messages and leads inside WordPress
  • New: AI Agent health — warns when the selected agent is untrained, paused, or has been deleted on Botvee
  • New: WooCommerce status panel, plus optional browse-abandonment and cart-recovery tracking (off by default)
  • New: live stock endpoint so Stock Alerts check real inventory before notifying a customer
  • Fixed: the dashboard showed the raw agent ID instead of its name until the agent list finished loading
  • Fixed: the proxy’s authentication failure response disclosed part of the stored shared secret and its length
  • Fixed: the shared secret and other options were left in the database after uninstall
  • Changed: plugin folder and text domain renamed from botvee-ai-chatbot to botvee-ai-agent
  • Changed: redesigned admin screen built around whether your AI Agent is actually live

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • OAuth-style authentication
  • AI Agent fetching and selection
  • Automatic widget injection
  • Encrypted token storage
  • Modern SaaS-style admin dashboard
